items.week_or_locator: lines 215-223 (history of accounting), 169-179 (regulators), 963-967 and 557-571 (2016 dates), 1307-1389 (April 2016)
items.objective: Verify and date every historical, legal and regulatory claim in the 1st Term Financial Accounting source before a lesson adopts it, and keep the source wording distinct from the corrected fact. At least: Luca Pacioli and the double entry system 'in 1494' (217); the royal charter to the Royal Niger Company 'in 1886' (217); the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria established '1st September, 1965' (219); the Association of National Accountants of Nigeria established '31st July, 1979' 'as the second professional accounting body in Nigeria' (219); the regulator set 'CBN, NDIC, SEC, CAC, NSE' and the tax bodies 'LSBIR' and 'FBIR' (169-179); the 2016 illustration dates ('July 2016' at 559, 'Trial Balance as at 31st July, 2016' at 923, 'April 2016' at 1311). Each claim must be checked against an authoritative primary source (statute, gazette, institute record or official history) and either confirmed with a citation or flagged as unverified; the year, the name and the ordinal claim ('second') are checked separately. Dated illustrations are presented as dated, never as current law, rates or statistics. If a source cannot be consulted in the run, record that limitation and leave the claim flagged rather than inventing a citation. Do not edit the source text.

items.week_or_locator: lines 559-718 and 843-953 and 1307-1631: the worked answers of Week 4-5, Week 6-7 and Week 9-10
items.objective: Re-check every worked answer in the 1st Term Financial Accounting source by reading and arithmetic before a lesson adopts it, and record a verdict per figure. The reviewed computations are: Week 4-5 postings (Cash 50,000 + 14,000 against 8,500 + 9,600 + 6,000 giving 39,900; Purchases 38,100; Sales 41,000; Returns Inwards 3,000; Returns Outwards 7,000; creditors 13,000; debtors 24,000; Fittings 6,000), the balance at 64,000/64,000 and the trial balance at 111,000 debit and 111,000 credit (931-953); Week 9-10 purchases journal 313,200 + 839,000 + 1,118,600 = 2,270,800, sales journal 289,400 + 402,800 = 692,200, returns outwards 55,080 + 111,350 = 166,430, returns inwards 68,400 + 21,375 = 89,775, and the cash book totals 201,000/239,000 with balances 168,000/164,900. Two specific issues must be resolved by reading, not assumed: the Returns Outwards account dates the S. Dauda entry 'Jul 12' (665) while the transaction (566) and the S. Dauda account (677) date it 21 July; and the N8,400 sundry-expenses cheque sits in an undetermined cash-book column in the flattened text, where the printed totals place it in the Bank column. Record for each figure whether it agrees, disagrees or cannot be read from the extraction, and hand any disagreement to the owner rather than silently correcting it. Do not declare a test suite passed; no suite is run.

items.objective: Record and bound the external textbook material named by the 1st Term Financial Accounting source, which was not supplied. The reading assignments are 'Simplified and Amplified Financial Accounting Page 1 - 7' (239), 'Page 16 - 17' (321), 'Page 41' (495), 'page 20 - 27' with 'Business Accounting 1 page 21 - 38' (759-761), and 'page 80 - 94' with 'Business Accounting 1 page 37 - 48' (989-991); the exercise references are 'Business Accounting 1 by Frank Wood, Exercise 3.6, 3.9A and 3.10A' (753), 'Business Accounting 1 Exercise 3.11 A' (869) and 'Simplified and Amplified Financial Accounting Exercise 7, 8x and 9' (983). Neither textbook is part of the supplied archive. Record the exact references and locators, and the rule that no lesson may claim, quote or paraphrase the content of those pages, and that an exercise depending on them is either given an original equivalent or recorded as unavailable pending the owner. Keep the two titles distinct and do not guess an author or edition for 'Simplified and Amplified Financial Accounting'. Do not download or commit either book.
